To find the lowest common multiple of three numbers, we first find their prime factorizations. 

- We start by finding the prime factorization of $21.$ We easily deduce that $21=3\cdot 7.$

- Next, we find the prime factorization of $28:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14167412/assets/502509ed3e4392c8c4e3e8fa0b0e579c096f0b04108091f4d18a6f0e5a879e2a.png)

Therefore, $28={2}^{2}\cdot 7.$

- Then, we find the prime factorization of $24:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14167412/assets/cbf192e5a1a1b1ac9db41bb9c8427ff8cdebeb697bcb618da87689a628b8f3af.png)

Therefore, $24={2}^{3}\cdot 3.$

So, we have the following prime factorizations:

$$
\begin{aligned}21 & =3\cdot 7 \\ 28 & ={2}^{2}\cdot 7 \\ 24 & ={2}^{3}\cdot 3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we write down every prime factor that is shown above, and we raise each prime factor to the highest power given in any of the factorizations:

- the highest power of $2$ is $3$

- the highest power of $3$ is $1$

- the highest power of $7$ is $1$

Therefore, the lowest  common multiple of $21$, $28$  and $24$ is 

$$
\text{LCM}(21,28,24)={2}^{3}\cdot 3\cdot 7=168.
$$
